subject: Pre-billing trigger, PO acknowledgement conditions & discount slab validation
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medcore.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Jacobs <tom.j@medcore.com>, ProcurementOps <procure@medcore.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T12:03:00Z
Subject: Pre-billing trigger request for upcoming PO

Hi Kimberly,

We're getting our finance and ERP team lined up to onboard Redwood for the Q3 commit. Before we issue the formal PO we need confirmation on two items to satisfy our internal controls:

1) PO acknowledgement: Is a signed PO acknowledgement required on your side, or will the presence of an approved PO number in the invoice header suffice? Our system enforces PO matching and we prefer a header-level PO id.

2) Pre-billing trigger / invoice cadence: We expect quarterly invoicing aligned with milestone acceptance. However, we want a pre-billing trigger to be able to generate a release notice 10 business days prior to the invoice run so our treasury can reserve funds. Can Redwood provide a pre-invoice notice (email + API webhook) and include a committed invoice window (e.g., invoice dated on first business day of quarter)?

Separately, our procurement team is evaluating the discount slab you offered — they need the slab logic documented (thresholds, effective dates, and whether credits are pro-rated if the PO is split across entities). I've attached our PO template for reference.

Can you confirm point-of-contact and whether any redlines to the PO template will be accepted, or if MedCore should follow your standard PO header format?

Thanks,

Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement, MedCore Solutions
elena.rossi@medcore.com
+44 20 5555 0123

Attachment: PO_Template_MedCore.pdf (stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medcore.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Pre-billing trigger request for upcoming PO

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the template. Quick responses inline below, and looping in Finance and Sales so we can land the operational details.

1) PO acknowledgement: Our standard practice is to accept an ERP PO number in the invoice header as proof of authorization. We can also return an automated acknowledgement when we receive the PO (PDF confirmation) if your process requires it. Which do you prefer?

2) Pre-billing trigger / invoice cadence: We can provide a pre-invoice notice by email and an API webhook feed to a configurable endpoint. We typically send the notice 7 business days before invoice generation; we can extend to 10 business days for an enterprise onboarding. Invoice dates can be fixed to the first business day of the quarter per your request.

3) Discount slab and pro-ration: Our discount slabs are threshold-based and applied on committed spend per contract entity. If a PO is split across legal entities, discounts are applied per-entity unless you request consolidated billing. Credits for partial quarters are pro-rated based on active days during the billing window. I've attached the Discount_Slab_Proposal.xlsx with the exact thresholds and sample calculations.

Next steps: Vivek, can you confirm the billing header fields we need to enforce (PO number, cost center, legal entity) and whether we can support 10 business day pre-invoice webhook? Vanessa — would you like to own a short SOW that captures invoice cadence and acknowledgement SLA?

Best,

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: Discount_Slab_Proposal.xlsx (stub)

From: Tom Jacobs <tom.j@medcore.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medcore.com>, ProcurementOps <procure@medcore.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T07:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Pre-billing trigger request for upcoming PO

On Fri, Jun 11, 2027 at 09:22 Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the template. Quick responses inline below, and looping in Finance and Sales so we can land the operational details.
>
> 1) PO acknowledgement: Our standard practice is to accept an ERP PO number in the invoice header as proof of authorization. We can also return an automated acknowledgement when we receive the PO (PDF confirmation) if your process requires it. Which do you prefer?

Thanks Kimberly — our ERP requires a header-level PO match, but the acknowledgement PDF as a secondary record would be helpful for our AP team.

Regarding the webhook: our security team will only accept webhook endpoints behind a vendor firewall; can you provide HMAC signing on the webhook payload and a rolling key rotation schedule? If that's difficult, an SFTP pre-invoice file drop is an acceptable alternative.

Finally, one small ask on the discount slab: can you include an example where a mid-quarter amendment increases committed spend (we need to show pro-rated credit calculations for our auditors). A single example row in the Excel would suffice.

Tom Jacobs
Corporate Treasury, MedCore Solutions
+44 20 5555 0199

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Tom Jacobs <tom.j@medcore.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medcore.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Pre-billing trigger request for upcoming PO

Tom / Elena — appreciate the detail. Short update and action items: 

- PO acknowledgement: We'll accept PO number in invoice header as the authoritative matching field and will also produce an automated acknowledgement PDF on receipt. MedCore confirmed preference noted.

- Webhook security: We support HMAC-signed webhook payloads (SHA256) and can rotate keys quarterly. If MedCore prefers SFTP drop, we can support that as a fallback; please indicate which you want in the final onboarding checklist.

- Discount slab example: Attached a new tab in Discount_Slab_Proposal.xlsx showing a mid-quarter amendment scenario with pro-rated credit calculations and journal entry example for auditors.

Action items: 
1) Elena: confirm whether you want consolidated billing across entities or per-entity discounts (this changes threshold application).
2) Tom / ProcurementOps: confirm webhook vs SFTP and provide endpoint details if webhook.
3) Vanessa: I'll coordinate a short SOW and include billing header enforcement and pre-invoice SLA (10 business days).

I'll prepare the PO acknowledgement template and we can send a final SOW + onboarding checklist once MedCore confirms the three items above.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198
